subject: Combining distance and time removal methods?

messages.author: 88330b77176627c3
messages.subject: Combining distance and time removal methods?
parts:
Hi-
 
I wanted to run this by the group just to make sure I'm not missing something.
 
I have single-visit point count data where observers estimated time to detection and distance.  In order to account for both availability and detection to estimate density (e.g., Farnsworth et al. 2005), I 'd like to combine the two methods - which isn't a currently available combo in unmarked - I don't believe.

So, to get at that, I could use a 2-staged process by first running a removal-type analysis (multinomPois) and then using those predicted counts to input into a distance analysis (distsamp)?  I would then include covariates on abundance into the second analysis and use those estimates of density (the ultimate objective).  Does that sound appropriate?
 
Thanks!

Courtney

I'm not entirely sure how to code for time-to-detection.  Any sample code out there?

Thanks,

messages.author: b2bc3c8f70c34410
messages.subject: Re: Combining distance and time removal methods?
parts:
Hi Jason, 
You might need to choose between using distance models and time removal models with unmarked (see gdistsamp, gmultmix functions). The R package 'detect' provides another option to model abundance and detection using both distance and time removal data (see cmulti function), but you may need to bootstrap for CIs, and I think the package provides a function to bootstrap. 

There is an example of a time removal analysis using the gmultmix function in unmarked in the documentation (here).
Cheers,
Brian
